A brief summary of what has been occupying my mind lately. Today I came across Girlhood’s new song 'buligyilkos'. While listening to it I started reflecting on many different things, and I felt it was worth writing a small note about it.So I began thinking that Azahriah might be one of the best examples if we are looking for an artist from here who is roughly my age. With someone like that it becomes very clear that when two people grow up listening to the same international artists, it naturally creates a certain collective connection between them. I often feel that this shared musical background quietly links me with many of my contemporaries.First I would like to say a few words about the producer behind this new Girlhood song. In my opinion he is one of the most outstanding producers in the current Hungarian music scene. I first encountered his name in connection with a Halloween themed song in 2023, and even then I considered his work exceptional. In one recurring section the new track reminds me very strongly of a passage from the band’s song 'közöny', perhaps even a little too strongly. Still, it is almost impossible to feel any resentment toward this band. In Hungary they might be the only act with a female vocalist whose voice and lyrics consistently make me smile, ever since their very first release.

As for everyday life, I had a meaningful experience at the end of last month when I was finally able to meet someone I know after a very long time. At the same time I have been thinking more and more sentimentally about the passage of time and about the simple fact that everything is finite. Because of this, certain experiences now appear in a completely different perspective, one that feels much richer in value.

Those who know me are aware that the reason my content has been quiet for quite some time is not only because the level of musical quality I am capable of has changed dramatically, or because the musical voice and structure through which I want to express myself have finally matured. The truth is that I am not entirely at peace with myself yet. Since March 1 I have been following a rather brutal new training routine and diet. It is something I had tried to establish for a long time without success, but now an interesting new circumstance has emerged. The negative thoughts, certain experiences, and the feeling that the thing I love the most in the world, releasing my music, seems to be moving further and further away from me, affect me emotionally to such an extent that they feel far more difficult to bear than simply accepting this new lifestyle.

So today marks day sixteen. Perhaps what weighed on me a little more today is the realization that the road ahead still seems very long. Yet at least I am already on that road. On the road toward the moment when I can finally invite all of you into my world through my new music and videos, and share the many stories and thoughts that live inside me through my compositions and my paintings. Simply being able to live that reality will make me happier than anything else, so in the end it will be worth it.

I have decided that I will actually start using this thing the way it was meant to be used, as a journal. After all, this is exactly why I created this page in the first place. If it is going to be personal, then so be it. Especially since in the future I will mostly communicate through music and music videos anyway, and for that small percentage of my audience who are more curious about what is happening behind the music, this page might finally serve a real purpose. From now on, whatever occupies my mind, whatever thoughts are present in me, I will write them down here.

Let me start with my theory: I believe that a person’s core musical taste is formed around the age of fifteen or sixteen. What you feel at that time, the emotional state you are in, and the music you listen to then will stay with you throughout your entire life, whether you want it to or not. I am convinced there is a strong connection between first loves and the music you listen to during the period in which you experience them. I find it very strange that since covid began, and throughout the entire period that followed, which is unsettling to realize has now grown longer than the time before it, everything feels strangely insignificant, almost meaningless. But before going there, I want to jump back to 2014–2015 and to my theory of music as a kind of time capsule. Back then, I was going through my first serious breakup, a period I can tie very clearly to listening to Guns N’ Roses albums. Then in 2017 I listened obsessively to Twenty One Pilots’ ‘Blurryface’, together with a girl with whom I had an unfulfilled relationship. Lately I have been thinking about how strange it is that at a certain age, the limitations imposed by youth, obligations, and the lack of independence can completely destroy a long-distance relationship. After that came a period defined by Billie Eilish, Bring Me The Horizon, and Falling In Reverse. One part of that era I owe to a friendship that still exists today, and another part to a very deep wound that followed me for a long time after a relationship that lasted exactly two weeks. Funny, isn’t it.

Then came university, and a very special relationship, the last one I would truly call special, which ended with the beginning of covid. I will be honest, I had to pause for a moment while writing this. It feels strange how often this period comes back to me lately, especially while listening to Badflower’s ‘OK, I’M SICK’, or to the band I discovered because of her, Cigarettes After Sex. It is remarkable what music combined with a unique life situation is capable of. Even after several years, images appear vividly before my eyes: parking my car in a terrible spot by the roadside because it was impossible to drive any further, then walking up those slightly castle-like paths while ‘Heroin’ plays, or simply recalling moments of uncomplicated happiness. How strange it is how much significance there once was in waking up next to someone, when that was not an everyday occurrence. And now, when one has independence and could do this at any time, how completely that significance has faded. I do not know what the problem is. Has it simply lost its meaning, or are experiences themselves no longer special? Or is it that when you experience something truly special for the first time, you do not fully understand it, and it can never happen in the same way again because this is how the human brain works. My personality has undergone something close to a complete reversal, and it is almost ironic that what I once disliked and could not live with is now exactly what I search for relentlessly in a woman. I want someone who is as devoted to something as I am to my music, someone who relentlessly pursues her dreams. Because, as the years have shown me, no other kind of personality can ever truly come close to understanding what goes on inside me, or how I function.
